body: Linux batch gate on head 3fa2631c: 0 failed - geometry, cl, tools, post, sim (132 s), motion incl. the slow finish3d/flow/pivot5d (129 s), app incl. center_cut_multiaxis (559 s), ui suites (64 s), clippy -D warnings (17 s); 15.1 min wall. Quick gate (sim + motion posed_subtract + app stock_export/verify) and app's heavy stock_engine_agreement lane in release were green locally before the push (see the body).

Back to draft: the review found a blocker. `march_up`'s `phi == 0` exit under-reports a flipped floor when a stock plane sits on a cell centre, and lifting E2a's refusal exposes it. Details, a reproducer and the suggested fix are in the review comment above.

Review fix pushed: dc4873e7 (`fix(sim): the field marches walk cell centres with exact signs, never points`). The PR stays a draft.

### The blocker, and what the trace showed underneath it
The `phi == 0 => Floor(z)` exits in `march_up` (`:111` and `:120`) are gone, and so is their twin in `march` (`march.rs:241`, #824) - the fix is one shared helper, so it is folded in here with `Refs #824` (the main session decides whether #824 closes on it). Following the review's sweep further, the exits were one of three holes with the same root, all in both marches:

1. **The on-surface exit** (the finding): a probe's magnitude is the cell's, so a cell whose centre lies on a stock plane reads zero at every point of the cell, and the exit answered whatever height the trace had reached (6.05 for the reviewer's scenario).
2. **The step from a point between centres.** The sphere trace stepped by the cell's magnitude from wherever it stood. A band value can over-read the truth by up to sqrt(3) cells (`field_gen`'s construction law), so from the lower half of a cell the landing could pass a web thinner than a cell and the climb then read the body below it.
3. **The "last air probe" fallback.** Where the landing cell's centre was air, `refine`/`refine_down` answered the last probe that read air. Under a cut claim that is no proof: a claim proves the centre and its half-line, not the cell's other half, so that probe can stand in material (in the reviewer's scenario the ascent's last "air" probe is in the cut cell's upper half, above the tool's top at 5.8 - "refine from the cell" alone would have kept the under-report).

### The fix
One `march::walk` shared by both directions. It visits cell centres only, with the exact parity-and-claim sign at each (`sign_at`: `parity_of` at the centre, the half-open `[floor, top)` law - a centre on a floor plane is material, one on a top plane is air - and `cut_at > 0` is removed). From an air centre it skips only a run the field proves air: a centre outside the shell proves its magnitude's cells less two; a claimed centre proves its claim's cells (a lower bound on the depth). The first material centre met is the stock's own end, the centre before it is air, and the surface is read from that one-cell bracket by `face` (the record's entry and the shell crossing, unchanged). `refine`, `refine_down`, `probe`, `STEP_MIN` and `MAX_MARCH_STEPS` are gone; `march_up` is a 70-line mirror through the same walk. The sliver scan's upper bound follows the same law (`center < ceiling`: a centre ON the ceiling is already the one above it), which is what lets the reviewer's scenario read exactly through the record instead of refusing.

Safety argument, in the module doc: every skipped centre is air by one of the two proofs, so no material centre is passed; the bracket's air end is proven and its material end exact; the read is the record (errs toward material) or the crossing (exact), or `Unreadable`. No point probe, no fallback height.

E2a's `bounded_cuts` on a flipped bake stays lifted - the walk is the proof the review asked for, not the refusal.

### Pins (`crates/sim/tests/field_floor.rs`)
- `a_stock_plane_on_a_cell_centre_reads_exactly_on_both_sides`: the reviewer's scenario (`cube((0,0,-6.25),(20,12,0))`, slot r 2 at -5.8, flipped) reads `Material { top: 6.25, floor: 5.8 }` to 1e-9 (was `{ 6.4406, 6.05 }`); #824's upright twin (slot at -6.0) reads `{ -6.0, -6.25 }` (was `{ -6.25, -6.25 }`); the uncut plate both ways (the old flipped top was 6.4406); a top on a centre (0.25) flipped with its slot.
- `no_column_under_reports_across_plates_and_slots_on_and_off_the_lattice`: the review's sweep - floors {-6, -6.25, -6.1, -6.3} x tops {0, 0.25, -0.2} x slot depths {floor -0.5 .. +1.5, nine of them}, under the slot and beside it, upright and flipped: **432 reads, every one exact, none under-read** (the assert is "covered or refused by name, never under"; the exact count is pinned at >= 90% so a drift toward refusal shows). On an 8 x 6 plate so the binary stays ~10 s in debug.
- Both fail on the old marches (checked by stashing the source and keeping the tests: the sweep's first on-centre config reads `[-6.25, -6.25]` under `[-6.25, -6.2]`).

Decision record: `docs/decisions/780-field-march-up.md` (the review-fix entry, with what was considered and dropped - the review's "refine from the cell", restoring the refusal, a safe float step, fixing `march_up` alone).

Every existing suite reads the same floats: the bracket read is unchanged, only the way to the bracket is. Linux quick gate against the previous head 3fa2631c (this diff's base; the stack's base ref is not on that box): sim suites, motion suites, app suites - 0 failed, 1.9 min wall.

Review fix 2 pushed: 03437938 (`fix(sim): a centre-less floor skin is a verdict on every march path, never NaN`). The PR stays a draft.

### The blocker
`walk` answered `NoMaterial` for a column whose skin held no cell centre, and every reader that marches alone (`Stock::top`, `deviate`, `measure`, the sheet, `Columns::top_at`/`above`) took it as NaN. Only `column_span` read such skins, through `field_floor::sliver`.

### The fix (`march.rs`, `field_floor.rs`)
- `march::walk` reads the centre-less column itself before it ever answers "no material", through the ONE sliver law: `field_floor::sliver` is now `pub(crate)` and called from the new `march::centreless` with the shell's extent from the shared `field_floor::shell_extent` (no copy). The outcomes:
  - the shell never crosses the column -> `NoMaterial` (air beside the stock);
  - the records place the sliver -> `Top(top)` for a descent, `Top(floor)` for an ascent;
  - the records prove every pair cut through -> `NoMaterial`;
  - the sliver cannot be placed, or a bounded tool claimed it -> `Unreadable`, never `NoMaterial` where the shell says material stands.
- The mesh-only walk (`cuts == false`, `measure_field`'s own-top read) answers the shell's highest crossing (descent) or lowest (ascent), exact for any plane.
- `column_span`'s `NoMaterial => sliver` arm becomes `Empty` (the walk has read the sliver); its `cut_near(floor)` refusal by name is unchanged, and the sliver's own `CutFromBelow` maps to `Unreadable` inside the walk.
- The older NaN reads (a floor on a boundary, -6.0, cut to -5.8) are the same code path and read now too.

### Pins (new suite `crates/sim/tests/field_skin.rs`, through the VERDICT path)
- `a_floor_skin_under_a_slot_is_a_verdict_on_every_path`: the reviewer's scenario (8 x 6 plate -6.05..0, slot r 2 at -5.8, part `cube((0,0,-7),(8,6,-6))`): `Stock::top` under the slot reads -5.8 (was NaN); `Stock::deviate(part, 0.01)` has 0 NaN columns, 192 of 192 rest, dev 0.2 under the slot and 6.0 beside it (was: 128 NaN, rest_cells 64); every `Columns::top_at` finite, `above(-6.0)` holds the skin, `above(-5.8)` does not; flipped, `Stock::top` reads 6.05 and `column_span` `[5.8, 6.05]`; the older -6.0 / -5.8 skin reads -5.8; a cut-through column is still air on every path.
- `no_column_the_shell_proves_reads_nan_or_air_through_stock_top`: floors {-6.0, -6.05, -6.1, -6.2, -6.25, -6.3} x tops {0, 0.25, -0.2} x slot depths floor + {-0.5, 0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.45, 0.5, 0.75, 1.5} (skins 0.01-0.3 among them), under and beside the slot, upright and flipped, through `Stock::top` (4 reads) and the flipped `column_span` (2 reads), plus `Stock::deviate` against the plate's own bottom on every upright fixture (0 NaN columns, every column rest where the skin is thicker than the tolerance). Asserts: where the shell proves material the read is finite and at or above the truth; a refusal there is a failure. **1296 reads, 1296 exact.** On dc4873e7 the same sweep had 186 NaN reads where the shell proves material (every one under the slot - floors -6.0/-6.05/-6.1/-6.2 upright and flipped, -6.25 flipped only, -6.3 at the floor) and 81 `deviate` runs with NaN columns; 1110 of 1296 exact.
- Both fail on the unfixed source (checked by stashing `crates/sim/src` and keeping the tests). The two round-1 pins in `field_floor` stay green.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/780-field-march-up.md` (review fix 2: what was considered and dropped - the `column_span` fallback from `march`, over-reporting the ceiling where the sliver cannot be placed, a new `Read` arm for `CutFromBelow`).
